title: Message processing pipeline with a scripted model stand-in
description: This example sets up five messages and four prompt roles (extract, draft, polish, classify) with a deterministic stand-in function that simulates each role's output, including deliberate bugs for the controls to catch.

steps.description: Five messages arrive: three events (chess, hawk hacks, ultimate frisbee), one question about library hours, and one announcement about free pizza.
CONFIG holds the settings you own: spawn_budget, temperature, and seed. These stay outside any prompt.

Four system prompts define the roles: EXTRACT pulls structured event lines, DRAFT writes a friendly digest, POLISH edits for concision and warmth, CLASSIFY labels each message as event, change, or question.
The EVENT regex parses lines that match 'name meets/is/moved to day at time in/on place', capturing the four fields.
CALLS tracks every model call so each pattern's cost can be counted.
stand_in is a scripted replacement for a language model. It implements fixed rules for each system prompt so every intermediate output is visible and repeatable.
For EXTRACT, the regex runs on each line and outputs matching events as 'name | day | time | place' lines.
For DRAFT, each extracted row becomes a sentence: 'name is on day at time (place).' All sentences are joined with spaces.
For POLISH, two deliberate bugs: ' is on ' becomes ': ' and 'Thursday' becomes 'Friday' — the mistake Question 6 warned about.
For CLASSIFY: 'moved' or 'cancel' means change; ends with '?' means question; matches EVENT means event; otherwise 'announcement' — a label outside the closed set.
llm is the single function every pattern calls. It logs the system prompt prefix to CALLS and delegates to stand_in.
The script prints the message count and CONFIG.
Two test calls: CLASSIFY on the first message returns 'event'; EXTRACT on the first message returns 'Chess club | Thursday | 7pm | Olin 107'. CALLS is then cleared for the next stage.
